patient_overview.name: Lesli Armstrong
patient_overview.description: Lesli Armstrong is a 43-year-old single woman from Newark who works part-time and was flagged at her last wellness visit with prediabetes and obesity, on top of a scoliosis diagnosis she's had since she was a teenager. She is stoic and tends to downplay everything — aches, stress, even her blood sugar numbers — and will change the subject if a question gets too close to money or how she's really doing. She's reached a point where she's decided she wants to do something about her blood sugar, but she needs the student to hand her one clear, doable first step rather than a long list.

demographics.occupation: Part-time receptionist at a dental office
demographics.cultural_context: Lesli grew up in Newark in a working-class household where you "didn't make a fuss" about aches and pains, and that attitude has stuck with her into adulthood. She was raised Baptist and still attends services most Sundays at a small congregation a few blocks from her apartment; the church's Wednesday potluck and prayer group are the main fixed points of her week and the people she trusts most. She doesn't tie her eating habits to any particular cultural cuisine — her food choices are shaped more by what's cheap, quick, and available near the bus line than by heritage.
